title: lint: field-no-consumers treats a field permission's `when` row condition as a carrier, so a field read only by that condition is flagged
body:
domain:spec#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzh7cM8EmUX4T2CBNHX

## What is wrong

A field permission's `when` (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`, the field-permission arm) is a CEL row condition. It is evaluated on the stored row before an update, so a lock such as `status in [...]` reads `status`. `field-no-consumers` (`packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.ts`) still treats every path under `permissions` as a carrier, apart from the RLS `using` / `check` predicates that #32256 (PR #32276) credits. So a field that only a field permission's `when` reads is reported as having no consumers.

This is the same false-positive class as #32256. #32256 left `when` as a carrier on purpose, because its card asked only for the RLS predicates. The contract review on PR #32276 (comment 6772543690) recommended this card.

## Ask

- Credit the fields named in a field permission's `when` as behaviour reads, the same way PR #32276 credits an RLS predicate. Type the key name against the spec schema, as that PR does (`satisfies`).
- The field the permission grants on stays a carrier. Only the condition's reads are credited.
- Pins: a field read only by a `when` is not reported; a field named only as a grant target still is. Ablate once.

Depends on PR #32276 landing first, because it shares the RLS credit's code path.
